prerequisites: Fulfill the requirements established by the University of Oviedo for bilingual programs (for students taking the course in English)
Minimum knowledge of the English language (recommended for students taking the course in Spanish, for practical activities with computer programs and understanding some readings)

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to direct activities that are the object of engineering projects.
Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to organize and plan in the field of business, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a team.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Model and solve problems related to the business system.
Make decisions related to production management.

teaching_methods: Assignment of topic-related practices (exercises, proposed problems, and resolution recommendations)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and practical blocks. The theoretical block grade is calculated as 0.65 multiplied by the theoretical exam (T1) score. The practical block grade is calculated as 0.35 multiplied by the average of the four practical exams (P1+P2+P3+P4)/4. The final grade is the sum of the theoretical and practical block grades. If the minimums for each block are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, there is a theoretical exam and a practical exam, both requiring a minimum score of 4 out of 10. The final grade is calculated as (0.65 * Theoretical Exam) + (0.35 * Practical Exam), with a minimum of 4.0 if minimums are not met. Differentiated assessment for part-time students replaces practical activities with a single individual practical test, maintaining other ordinary call conditions.
